title: Function as the Basis of Psychiatric Ward Design
limitations: Theoretical paper with no empirical data collection
Based on clinical observation rather than controlled experimentation
No quantitative measures or statistical analysis

extraction_metadata.notes: This paper is a foundational architectural design manual for psychiatric wards. It is not an empirical study and contains no quantitative findings. It presents design principles based on clinical experience and theoretical reasoning rather than experimental evidence. The paper discusses how schizophrenic patients' perceptual disturbances (particularly spatial perception anomalies documented by Weckowicz in an accompanying note) should inform architectural design decisions.
extraction_metadata.validation: JSON validated. No findings to extract—paper is theoretical/prescriptive.

key_design_principles_discussed.basis: Clinical observation; animal studies showing adrenal changes under overcrowding
key_design_principles_discussed.architectural_implication: Limit numbers in shared spaces to avoid forced proximity

key_design_principles_discussed.basis: Undesirable effects on mentally ill who lose hope of recovery
key_design_principles_discussed.architectural_implication: Avoid large congregate spaces; use small group organization

key_design_principles_discussed.principle: Provision of a Path of Retreat
key_design_principles_discussed.basis: Physical retreat less harmful than psychological withdrawal
key_design_principles_discussed.architectural_implication: Design escape routes; private spaces essential

key_design_principles_discussed.basis: Reference to Hediger's animal research on den/nest importance
key_design_principles_discussed.architectural_implication: 50-100 sq ft private rooms; preferable to larger dormitory spaces

key_design_principles_discussed.basis: Groups of 4-8 people form supportive relationships
key_design_principles_discussed.architectural_implication: Small group dormitories with bed alcoves rather than 2-3 bed rooms

key_design_principles_discussed.basis: Mentally ill find ambiguity intolerable; well people respond with tension
key_design_principles_discussed.architectural_implication: Clear labeling; simple, unambiguous environments; avoid confusing corridors

key_design_principles_discussed.basis: Mental hospitals reverse normal choice patterns; too many intimate choices, too few everyday choices
key_design_principles_discussed.architectural_implication: Allow everyday choice (food, clothing); limit forced intimate relationships
Personalize living spaces; allow decoration and self-expression

key_design_principles_discussed.basis: 100-year segregation policy harms schizophrenics uncertain about sexual identity
key_design_principles_discussed.architectural_implication: Mixed-gender wards; interaction with opposite sex essential for social skills

perceptual_disturbances_referenced.source: Weckowicz accompanying note on perceptual world of schizophrenic patients

disturbances.manifestation: Size constancy disordered; retinal image dominates; over-estimate distance; perceive larger subjective space
disturbances.architectural_consequence: Large spaces and corridors harmful; circular spaces preferable to rectangular; small, clearly defined environments required

disturbances.manifestation: Frequent auditory hallucinations, voices; distressing echoes
disturbances.architectural_consequence: Avoid disturbing echoes; good acoustics essential

disturbances.manifestation: Disturbances leaving patients puzzled about temporal location
disturbances.architectural_consequence: Ample clocks, calendars, up-to-date newspapers; TV and internal broadcast systems to anchor real time

disturbances.manifestation: Interest in texture; sensitivity to coarse institutional materials
disturbances.architectural_consequence: Pleasant-textured fabrics and surfaces; quality linens and tableware
Well-ventilated spaces; sufficient number of properly functioning toilets

disturbances.manifestation: Alarming disturbances of bodily image; related to hypochondriacal delusions
disturbances.architectural_consequence: Good surroundings reduce preoccupation; mirrors for self-orientation (under patient control)
